content: On July 11, 2022, a study was conducted comparing the effects of Remdesivir versus standard of care (SOC) or placebo in the treatment of COVID-19. The following findings were presented using forest plots to analyze various outcomes: 1. All-cause mortality: A forest plot was generated to compare the impact of Remdesivir versus SOC or placebo on overall mortality rates among COVID-19 patients. This analysis aimed to determine whether Remdesivir reduced the risk of death compared to standard treatments or placebo. 2. New need for mechanical ventilation or ECMO: Another forest plot evaluated the likelihood of patients requiring mechanical ventilation or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) when treated with Remdesivir versus SOC or placebo. This outcome assessed the progression of respiratory failure in patients. 3. Clinical improvement: A separate forest plot analyzed the rate of clinical improvement in patients treated with Remdesivir compared to those receiving SOC or placebo. This outcome measured the recovery trajectory and overall health improvement. 4. Serious adverse events: The study also included a forest plot examining the incidence of serious adverse events in patients treated with Remdesivir versus SOC or placebo. This analysis was critical in evaluating the safety profile of Remdesivir. 5. Discharge: Another forest plot assessed the rate of hospital discharge among patients treated with Remdesivir compared to SOC or placebo. This outcome provided insights into the time to recovery and readiness for discharge. 6. Hospitalization or death: The final forest plot compared the combined outcome of hospitalization or death in patients treated with Remdesivir versus SOC or placebo. This analysis aimed to evaluate the overall effectiveness of Remdesivir in reducing severe outcomes. These analyses were conducted using Review Manager (RevMan) version 5.4.1, a software tool commonly used for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Each outcome was carefully examined to provide a comprehensive understanding of the efficacy and safety of Remdesivir in the treatment of COVID-19.
